headings.title: The Global Scope of Professional Nursing
headings.content: Nursing is not restricted by national borders. Across the world, nurses share core values of care, safety, and advocacy, even though their local practices change depending on resources and culture. International professional nursing organizations connect these dispersed workforces, creating a unified voice for the profession. When nurses unite globally, they share best practices, respond faster to health emergencies, and tackle shared challenges like workforce shortages and burnout. These bodies remind individual practitioners that they belong to a massive worldwide community dedicated to human health.

headings.title: The International Council of Nurses (ICN)
headings.content: Founded in 1899, the **International Council of Nurses (ICN)** is a federation of more than 130 national nurses associations, representing millions of nurses worldwide. Run by nurses for nurses, ICN works to ensure quality nursing care for all, sound health policies globally, the advancement of nursing knowledge, and the presence of a respected, competent worldwide nursing profession. Through policy statements, congresses, and leadership programs, ICN shapes how governments view the nursing workforce.

headings.title: Setting Global Standards for Practice and Education
headings.content: International bodies establish benchmarks that guide training institutions and clinical settings. These standards cover ethical conduct, professional practice scopes, and educational requirements. By defining what safe, competent nursing looks like globally, these organizations help countries with developing health systems elevate their training programs. This harmonization ensures that a nurse moving across borders meets recognized professional baselines.

headings.title: Advocating for the Workforce Worldwide
headings.content:
- **Workplace Safety**: Pushing for safe staffing levels, personal protective equipment, and freedom from violence.
- **Fair Remuneration**: Advocating for salaries that match the high skill, education, and risk involved in nursing.
- **Leadership Roles**: Demanding that nurses sit at policy-making tables where health decisions are finalized.

headings.title: Collaboration with the World Health Organization (WHO)
headings.content: International nursing organizations work closely with the **World Health Organization (WHO)** to tackle global health crises, maternal mortality, and non-communicable diseases. Because nurses make up the largest segment of the health workforce, WHO relies heavily on nursing leadership to achieve targets like Universal Health Coverage. Joint reports, such as the *State of the World's Nursing* report, provide governments with concrete data to justify investing in the profession.

headings.title: Impact on Nigerian Nursing Practice
headings.content: Nigerian nursing benefits directly from international engagement through the **Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria (NMCN)**, which aligns local standards with global benchmarks. Nigerian nursing leaders participate in international forums, bringing home strategies on curriculum reform, advanced practice nursing, and task-shifting policies. Engaging globally also helps highlight local struggles—such as brain drain and infrastructure deficits—on international stages, drawing global attention and support to Nigerian health challenges.
